facts: Fossils preserve remains, impressions, or traces of ancient organisms.
What is a dinosaur footprint fossil called?
Tracks record activity and are trace fossils.
Palaeontologists study ancient life using fossils and geology.
Where are older undisturbed rock layers usually found?
Superposition places older layers beneath younger ones.
Tooth shape and wear can suggest what an animal ate.
Coprolites can reveal diet and ancient ecosystems.
What can fossil dinosaur eggs tell scientists?
Eggs and nests provide evidence about reproduction and behaviour.
Which living animals are surviving dinosaurs?
Modern birds evolved from theropod dinosaurs.
When did non-avian dinosaurs go extinct?
The end-Cretaceous mass extinction occurred about 66 million years ago.
Which impact crater is linked to dinosaur extinction?
The Chicxulub impact is strongly linked to the end-Cretaceous extinction.
What did the Chicxulub impact likely cause?
Dust, aerosols, fires, and climate effects followed the impact.
In which period did the earliest dinosaurs appear?
The earliest known dinosaurs appeared in the Late Triassic.
The Jurassic followed the Triassic in the Mesozoic Era.
Which period ended with the non-avian dinosaur extinction?
The Cretaceous ended about 66 million years ago.
An animal that eats only meat
Herbivores feed mainly on plant material.
An animal that eats other animals
An animal that eats only plants
Carnivores feed mainly on other animals.
Tyrannosaurus rex belonged to which broad dinosaur group?
T. rex was a large theropod dinosaur.
What body plan is typical of sauropods?
Sauropods were large long-necked, long-tailed herbivores.
Triceratops is best known for what?
Triceratops had facial horns and a large frill.
Did some non-avian dinosaurs have feathers?
Fossils show feathers and feather-like structures in many theropods.
Can scientists estimate age from dinosaur bones?
Growth rings and bone microstructure can provide age estimates.
How can scientists date volcanic layers near fossils?
Radiometric methods can provide numerical ages for volcanic rocks.
Why are similar fossils found on continents now far apart?
Plate tectonics moved continents after many fossils formed.
What should scientists do when strong new fossil evidence conflicts with an old idea?
Scientific explanations change when reliable evidence changes.
Why are dinosaur reconstructions sometimes updated?
New fossils and analyses can change scientific reconstructions.
